newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian charged with extortion after food scare.
newsitem.headline: Australian charged with extortion after food scare.

text.p: A 33-year-old Australian man appeared in court on Wednesday charged with attempting to extort A$4.1 million (US$3.1 million) from Swiss-based international food giant Nestle in a food contamination scare.
Computer analyst Mark James Milton entered no plea at Sydney's Central Local Court after being charged with one count of demanding money with menaces.
The court was told Milton sent a letter to Nestle Australia on May 21 demanding that the money be placed in a bank account he had opened under a false name.
Over the following two days, the food company was notified by facsimile message that contaminated coffee and yoghurt had been placed on supermarket shelves in Sydney, the court heard.
Police removed the products and tests later showed they had been contaminated with pesticide.
Milton, who was arrested on Monday at his Melbourne home, was refused bail in a brief court appearance.
The case was adjourned until June 11.
Nestle Australia is a subsidiary of Nestle SA.
